uPAR is involved in a wide spectrum of brain diseases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

uPAR is a multifaceted protein, with multiple functions and a complex network of interactions that may play a key role in the central nervous systems, in the brain development, in the normal functioning, and in the pathophysiology of several neurological and psychiatric disorders.
uPAR is involved in many brain disorders.
the uPAR-related molecular network is a key player in the pathogenesis of epilepsy and other brain disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uPAR-related molecular network is a key regulator of neuronal development, of the functioning of the central nervous and of the brain's ability to process language.

uPAR and its ligands, and more generally the plasmin(ogen) activation system and its regulators and partners are involved in the central nervous systems, and that they are likely key players in the pathophysiology of epilepsy and of other neurological and psychiatric disorders.

the uPAR pathway represents an attractive target for novel therapeutic interventions, either in the context of epilepsy and other brain disorders, or in the context of developmental speech disorders and related disorders.
